title: feat(plugin-audit)!: sys_comment.reactions retires; a reaction lives only in sys_comment_reaction, and stored reactions are not migrated
body:
Fixes #22573
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

`sys_comment.reactions` retires under the maintainer's ruling A on #22505 as amended (record `6091550406`): 「同意;sys_comment.reactions 可以退役;可以不用考虑历史数据迁移;」. Per the director's judgment of the delegated point (`6091621568`), nothing takes its place on the comment row: no stored aggregate and no block computed on read. A reaction is its reactor's own `sys_comment_reaction` record, which landed in PR #22603. No stored reaction is migrated.

## What changed

- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment.object.ts`: the `reactions` field is gone. The docblock records the retirement, its reason and what an existing database keeps. The file surface is the one the claim names; the producer is this declaration, nothing else.
- The four generated translation bundles (`plugin-audit/src/translations/{en,es-ES,ja-JP,zh-CN}.objects.generated.ts`) drop the field's label. They were regenerated with `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write`, not edited by hand. Only the plugin-audit bundles moved.
- **Retirement record: an ADR-0087 D3 semantic entry**, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sys-comment-reactions-column-retired.ts`, on the protocol-18 step. This is a platform-object column, not an authorable spec key. So nothing goes into `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` (no spec schema ever declared the key) and there is no liveness-ledger row. That is the shape `position-permissions-column-retired`, `sys-job-organization-column-retired` and `sys-audit-log-organization-column-retired` already use. The gates decided this. `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` printed: `✓ check-adr-0087-registration: 1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition. .changeset/22573-sys-comment-reactions-retired.md [BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] registered sys-comment-reactions-column-retired (new here: sys-comment-reactions-column-retired)`. `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:api-surface` and `check:authorable-surface` are all green, and no generated spec artifact moved.
- `.changeset/22573-sys-comment-reactions-retired.md` covers `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/spec`, both `minor`. The `minor` follows the launch-window convention that `check-changeset-no-major` enforces, and the spec bump carries the new registry entry, which ships in `@objectstack/spec/migrations`. The changeset states that existing emoji reactions in the column are gone after the upgrade and that reactions now live in `sys_comment_reaction`. It gives a FROM → TO table and an operator sentence built from the measurements below.

## Measured: what the data door answers a write that still names the field

Showcase booted with `pnpm dev -- --fresh -p PORT --database file:SCRATCH/react.db` (`SqlDriver(better-sqlite3)`), signed in as the seeded admin, REST data door:

| request | before (base `45e206e49`) | after (this branch) |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `POST /api/v1/data/sys_comment` with `reactions` | `201`, map stored and returned | `400` `{"error":"Unknown field 'reactions' on object 'sys_comment'","code":"INVALID_FIELD","field":"reactions","object":"sys_comment"}`, nothing written |
| `PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_comment/ID` with `reactions` | `200`, map overwritten | `400 INVALID_FIELD`, same body |
| `GET /api/v1/data/sys_comment?reactions=x` | (not measured before) | `400 INVALID_FIELD` |
| `GET /api/v1/data/sys_comment/ID` (row holding a stored map) | `reactions` returned | `200`, no `reactions` key |
| `POST` without `reactions` | `201` | `201` |

**The after-reading is a loud refusal, not a silent drop.** It is the engine's undeclared-field preflight, which runs before any hook or driver. The door's handling of unknown fields is unchanged.

## Measured: what happens to the stored column (SQL driver)

The after-boot ran on the same sqlite file as the before-boot, which had a `reactions` column holding a stored map:

- **Schema sync leaves the column in place, values included.** I read `PRAGMA table_info('sys_comment')` after the boot. The column still holds the map written before the change.
- **The boot is clean.** One drift line, `[schema-drift] sys_comment.reactions: column exists in the database but not in metadata (orphaned) — "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it.`, and no error.
- **The named remedy works.** On a copy of the database, `os migrate plan` with an auth secret set lists `✗ sys_comment.reactions [drop_column]` as destructive, and `os migrate apply --allow-destructive --yes` drops it (`✓ Applied 1 change(s).`, column absent on re-read). Without an auth secret the plan composes no auth family, the audit plugin included. It then lists `sys_comment` under "declared by no object in this plan" and plans no drop. The plan prints that coverage gap itself, and the changeset's operator sentence says to run it with the audit plugin composed.
- No migration code was written.

## Census (re-done at `45e206e49`)

- The column was declared only in `sys-comment.object.ts` and labelled only in the four bundles. `packages/qa/dogfood`: 0 hits. `examples/`: 0 hits. `content/docs`: no page names the column; the hits are `enableReactions`, a UI prop, and the word "reactions" in prose.
- `packages/spec/src/api/discovery.test.ts:688` is `capabilities.comments.features.reactions`, a discovery capability flag in a fixture. It is not about this column.
- `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/key-mention.test.ts:177` uses the English word ("the two reactions available to the seat") in a comment about a ratchet. It is not about this column.
- `docs/adr/0052-audit-is-not-the-activity-feed.md:178` lists `reactions` among the fields `sys_comment` declared when that ADR was written. That is historical ADR text on a governed surface, and it is not edited here.

## Pins

- `plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment-retired-fields.test.ts`, new block "reactions stays retired":
  - `sys_comment` declares no `reactions` field, and no index, highlight or title names it.
  - The retirement record names it: `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].semantic` holds `sys-comment-reactions-column-retired`, its `surface` starts `sys_comment.reactions`, and its `replacement` names `sys_comment_reaction`.
  - The replacement exists: `sys_comment_reaction` declares `comment_id`, `emoji` and `user_id`.
- `plugin-audit/src/sys-comment-reactions-door.integration.test.ts` runs on a real engine with the real `AuditPlugin` and the sqlite-wasm driver. A create and an update naming `reactions` are refused: `mapDataError` gives `400` with `code` `INVALID_FIELD` and `field` `reactions`. No row is written, and the update's other key is not applied either. The control is the same create without `reactions`, which succeeds.
- **Ablation, done once on commit `330fc84c1`.** I ran `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (wrap mode, plus a shell trap that restores from `HEAD`), putting `reactions: Field.textarea(...)` back into the object. Anchor 1 → 0, blob `5364816272be` → `30c2ae8114be`. Three tests went red:
  - `× sys_comment declares no reactions field, and no index, highlight or title names it` — `AssertionError: sys_comment.reactions was retired — … expected [ 'id', 'thread_id', …(11) ] to not include 'reactions'`
  - `× create: 400 INVALID_FIELD naming reactions …` — `a create carrying reactions was accepted: expected undefined to be defined`
  - `× update: 400 INVALID_FIELD naming reactions …` — same
  - Restore: blob after restore `5364816272be` equals the blob at HEAD, `git diff HEAD` is empty, and an independent `git hash-object` agrees.
  - The first attempt was refused by the tool before any test ran (my anchor appeared inside the replacement, so the anchor count did not drop). It was a no-op, and I re-anchored on the retirement comment line.
- **The card's second pin, "the console at the bumped pin reacts through reaction records only", has no in-repo harness here.** The Console Pin Gate proves the pinned objectui SHA builds; it does not drive the chatter. No showcase smoke test or dogfood test mentions reactions. The evidence is the seat's reading of the console at pin `4997995022` (`6112978539` on #22500): `RecordDetailView.tsx` uses the `records` store whenever the deployment declares `sys_comment_reaction`, which this framework does. I did not invent a harness for it.

## Tests and gates (all at `f2825700c`, the final commit)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit test`: 47 files, 743 tests passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck`: exit 0, test layer included (`check:test-typecheck: OK`).
- `@objectstack/spec`: `vitest run --project local` 648 files / 19375 passed (1 todo); `--project repo` 55 files / 971 passed. Spec and plugin-audit were rebuilt before the runs.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (9 paths vs merge base `45e206e49`) derived 91 commands. All 91 ran and exited 0. `--ran` reconciliation: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 91 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 91 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`.
- `origin/main` has moved past the base: `3f694715e`, `63739521d`, `3fdb92db0`, `5ce6773a5`, `20028dfff`. None touches `plugin-audit`. The only spec file among them is a different migration entry, so I did not merge; the merge ref CI builds covers the join.

## Acceptance notes

- **A pending release note that becomes false.** `.changeset/22566-comment-reaction-record.md` (from PR #22603, not yet consumed: `.changeset/pre.json` lists no consumed changesets) ends with "`sys_comment.reactions` is unchanged in this release … It is retired separately". Both changesets are pending for the same release. I first corrected that bullet in place. `check-empty-changeset` then refused, as designed for somebody else's release note: "DELIBERATE CORRECTION … say so on the PR and get it confirmed; this gate stays red either way". So I restored the file byte-for-byte to the base (blob `d5ba5fd69f4f`). This PR's own changeset now says it supersedes that line. Whether to correct the sibling note too, with the gate red until a person confirms, or in a separate docs-only change, is the seat's call. The one-line replacement would be: "`sys_comment.reactions` is retired by a separate change on this line, which carries its own entry. Reactions stored in that column are not converted into records."
- An application that shows reactions still owes a `sys_comment_reaction` grant (read, create, delete). That was handed to the `repo:hotcrm` seat in `6094633923` and is not part of this PR.
- The claim's fences held: no change to `sys_comment_reaction`, its access hooks, its own-record floor, the author-only edit rule on `sys_comment`, or objectui.
